title: Pixum AI Review 2026: Sign Up or Stay Away?
description: Pixum AI review: what its promotional page claims, what we could verify, and the missing regulator, fee and deposit details to check before you sign up.
author: Sophia Reynolds
excerpt: Pixum AI makes automation and security claims, but its promotional page names no regulator, fees or deposit terms.
content:
Pixum AI describes itself as an automated trading platform for investors who want data-driven decisions. Its promotional page makes broad claims about machine learning, low-latency execution and security. Claims like these are easy to write and hard to check, so this review separates what the platform says from what we could verify.

The page is aimed at U.S. investors and ends with calls to action. It does not name an operator, a regulator or a licence number, and every link on it points to one external affiliate site.

Pixum AI at a Glance

Here is what the reference page states and what it leaves out.

Platform typeAutomated, AI-assisted trading platform
Target usersU.S. investors, from beginners to experienced traders
DevicesDesktop, tablet and phone (stated, not tested)
Minimum depositNot stated
FeesNot stated
Payment methodsNot stated
Support hoursNot stated
Regulator or licenceNot stated

Items marked as stated come from the platform's own page. We have not tested the platform.

The Main Claims, and What We Could Check

Automation and machine learning

The page says machine learning finds patterns that humans miss and that strategies are backtested against historical data. Backtesting is a common feature across this category, but a backtest shows how a strategy would have behaved in the past. It is not a forecast, and the page shows no results from live accounts.

Risk management

The page describes automated stop-loss and take-profit orders, plus what it calls intelligent allocation across holdings. These tools can limit losses on a single trade. They do not stop a portfolio from falling in a broad market move, and the page does not explain how the allocation works.

Security

The page mentions encryption, multi-factor authentication, real-time monitoring and security audits. It does not name the auditor, link to an audit report or state which regulator it complies with, so these claims cannot be checked from the page alone.

Costs Worth Knowing

The reference page gives no minimum deposit, fee schedule or withdrawal terms. Do not assume a fee-free account. Read the current terms, and check how withdrawals are handled, before you send money.

Our standard minimum deposit for this review is 250 in the reader's local currency: AUD 250 in Australia, GBP 250 in the UK and EUR 250 in the EU. Where the platform states a different figure, we show it alongside ours. Confirm the exact amount in its terms before you deposit.

Before You Register: A Short Checklist

  • Find the legal operator behind the platform and check it against your national regulator's register.
  • Look for an audit report or a named auditor, not just the word "audited".
  • Read the fee, deposit and withdrawal terms in full.
  • Use any demo account before you fund a live one.

Risks to Keep in Mind

An unclear operator is the main risk. Automation changes how trades are placed, not whether they can lose money. A promotional page that ends in urgent calls to action is a reason to slow down, not speed up.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does Pixum AI state a minimum deposit?

Not on its promotional page. Check the sign-up flow and the terms before you deposit anything.

Is Pixum AI regulated?

We could not confirm a regulator or licence number from the platform's own page. Search the regulator's register yourself.

Does Pixum AI charge fees?

Fees are not stated on the reference page. Read the current fee schedule before funding an account.

Does automation remove the risk of losing money?

No. Automated stop-loss and take-profit orders limit some losses, but they do not remove market risk.

Our Verdict on Pixum AI

Pixum AI makes strong claims with little to back them up. The reference page gives no regulator, fees or deposit terms, and its links all go to one affiliate site. We rate it at the lower end of our band until the operator and its terms can be verified. Start only with money you can afford to lose, and check everything yourself first.
